lines.label: Packaged terminal air conditioner, G.E., 208/1/60, in a through-wall sleeve - BOTH SCHEDULE MARKS ARE CARRIED. M201 schedules PTAC-2 = G.E. AZ65H15DAB (449/290 CFM hi-lo, OSA 45.0 CFM, 14,200 BTU/h cool, 13,300 BTU/h heat) and PTAC-1 = G.E. AZ65H12DAB (449/300 CFM, OSA 45.0 CFM, 11,900 cool, 10,400 heat)
lines.where: Exterior window wall under the window. 238's window bay splits 7'-1" / 6'-0" (GR-401 shade) / 3'-9 1/4" - asymmetric and unique to A556, so the sleeve is NOT on the standard-QQ centreline. ST-02 stone stool over the unit (A556 view 07).
lines.instanceNote: MARK IS UNRESOLVED AND BOTH ARE CARRIED (packages/mechanical.md flag F4, section 7). M401's guestroom detail for this room type is detail 02 'QQ Acc.', and M401's own text says details 01/02 show PTAC-2 - which puts PTAC-2 on 238. M201 schedules both marks. M302 says only that 'PTAC-2 is used on the higher-load room types' and names no room numbers. packages/mechanical.md section 7 therefore writes the whole QQ family, QQ Acc. included, as 'PTAC-2 / PTAC-1' with both models carried. The two units differ by 2,300 BTU/h cooling and 2,900 BTU/h heating - a wrong unit is a comfort complaint, not a paperwork error. SETTLES IT: read the PTAC tag off M302 in the field set for room 238, or read the installed nameplate. COUNT: one PTAC. M401 detail 02 draws a single unit, E103 row 11 carries a single 2080 VA PTAC load, and A556 view 01 places keynote 1 once - but A556 elevations 06 and 07 EACH carry keynote 1 twice, so count the units and record the number.
lines.src: M201 PTAC schedule (both rows verbatim) - M401 detail 02 'QQ Acc.' + KN3 + KN7 - M302 Mechanical Second Floor Plan - M501 detail 9 - A556 view 01 keynote 1 and view 07 (ST-02 stool) - E103 row 11 'Queen Queen ACC, CD' PTAC 2080 VA - packages/mechanical.md section 7 / flag F4
lines.verifyAtPunch: Read the nameplate and WRITE DOWN the model - AZ65H15DAB (PTAC-2) or AZ65H12DAB (PTAC-1) - and confirm 208/1/60; that reading is what closes flag F4 for this key. Then run heat, then run cool, from the wall control and confirm the unit responds each time with no rattle in the sleeve.

lines.label: PTAC wall sleeve kit (furnished with the unit) - caulked all around, bottom of sleeve min 3-1/4" AFF, plus the drywall closure that finishes the gap between the PTAC and the wall opening
lines.where: Through-wall at the exterior window wall, below the ST-02 stool.
lines.src: M201 PTAC notes ('wall sleeve kit') - M501 detail 9 ('wall sleeve furnished with unit, caulked all around ... min 3-1/4" AFF') - AS103 PTAC through-wall detail ('DRYWALL ENCLOSURE REQ'D. TO FINISH GAP BETWEEN PTAC AND WALL OPENING')
lines.verifyAtPunch: Run a finger around the sleeve perimeter inside and out - continuous caulk, no daylight, no whistle - and measure to the bottom of the sleeve against min 3-1/4" AFF (M501 det 9). Confirm the drywall closure at the sleeve-to-opening gap is finished and painted (AS103).

lines.label: PTAC exterior louver / architectural wall grille at the window wall
lines.where: Exterior face of the PTAC sleeve - visible from outside and, through the unit's outdoor section, from the room.
lines.instanceNote: FIVE STATEMENTS, NO RESOLUTION - MATERIAL, FINISH METHOD AND WHICH SUB BUYS IT ALL DISAGREE. M201 PTAC notes: 'wall sleeve kit + polypropylene louver kit (color by architect)'. M501 detail 9: 'aluminum architectural-style grille factory-painted to match exterior wall'. M401 KN1: 'architectural wall grille furnished with unit; grille painted to match exterior wall (typical for all PTAC units)'. A200 keyed note 8: 'ALUMINUM FIXED WINDOW ... WITH INTEGRAL ALUMINUM LOUVER AT PTAC UNITS' - i.e. the glazing sub's buy, not a PTAC accessory. AS103: integral louver installed with the window system. Polypropylene is moulded in colour, so M201's product and M401's paint instruction may be physically incompatible. SETTLES IT: one RFI to the M-EOR and MWT covering material, who paints it, and whose buy it is - and the approved G.E. PTAC accessory submittal. RECORD what is actually installed at 238; that observation is half the answer.
lines.src: M201 PTAC notes - M501 detail 9 - M401 KN1 - A200 keyed note 8 - AS103 - A556 view 07 (window wall elevation)
lines.verifyAtPunch: From outside: louver present, seated, fastened, blades straight, colour matching the elevation run. From inside: no daylight, no staining. WRITE DOWN the material you actually find (polypropylene or aluminium) and whether it is field-painted or factory-finished - the sheets give three answers and your reading is the field evidence.

lines.label: Interior architectural wall grille at the PTAC, painted to match the INTERIOR wall (M401 KN5)
lines.where: Room-side face of the PTAC / sleeve at the window wall, under the ST-02 stool.
lines.instanceNote: DB GAP - no row exists for this on 238. M401 prints two nearly identical keyed notes: KN1 'grille painted to match EXTERIOR wall (typical for all PTAC units)' and KN5 'grille painted to match INTERIOR wall'. The sheet does not say whether that is ONE grille whose two faces are painted two colours, or TWO grilles. It decides whether there is a separate painted grille inside the room to inspect and whose paint scope the room-side face is. SETTLES IT: same RFI as the exterior louver - ask the M-EOR whether KN1 and KN5 are one grille or two, and confirm who paints the room-side face and to which PT code.
lines.src: M401 KN5 against M401 KN1 - M501 detail 9 - A556 view 07
lines.verifyAtPunch: Look at the room-side face of the PTAC/sleeve and RECORD whether a separate grille is there; if it is, confirm it is fastened, undamaged and painted to the adjacent interior wall finish, and photograph it either way.

lines.label: PTAC drain kit (furnished with the unit) - M501 detail 9 calls it out for 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th-floor units, and 238 is a 2nd-floor unit
lines.where: At the PTAC base pan / sleeve, discharging to the condensate drain that runs down the wall.
lines.instanceNote: The piping downstream is PLUMBING scope (M401 KN2, M501 det 9) and is concealed in the wall - that run is dropped as rough-in. The kit itself and its performance are testable at the unit, which is why this line is IN.
lines.src: M501 detail 9 ('drain kit for 1st/2nd/3rd/4th-floor units, furnished with unit') - M401 KN2 - M301 General Note 6 - AS103
lines.verifyAtPunch: Run the PTAC in cooling long enough to make condensate, then look: water leaves through the kit, with nothing pooling in the base pan, weeping into the room, or staining the wall, carpet edge or the ST-02 stool below.

lines.label: PTAC fresh-air filter, MERV 13 or MERV 8, with bracket and gasket
lines.where: At the PTAC fresh-air / return-air path, behind the front grille.
lines.instanceNote: M201 itself offers 'MERV 13 or 8', so either is compliant on its face - do NOT write up a MERV 8 as a deficiency without checking the approved submittal, and do not assume MERV 13.
lines.src: M201 PTAC notes ('MERV 13 or 8 fresh-air filter w/ bracket & gasket') - M501 detail 9 (air filter + return-air path shown)
lines.verifyAtPunch: Lift the front panel: filter seated in its bracket with the gasket sealing and no bypass around the frame, clean, and RECORD the MERV number printed on the frame.

lines.label: PTAC fresh-air kit - the outside-air path delivering the scheduled 45.0 CFM OSA
lines.where: At the PTAC outdoor section, reachable by opening the unit front.
lines.instanceNote: M201's accessory sentence names BOTH a 'MERV 13 or 8 fresh-air filter w/ bracket & gasket' AND 'low-ambient + fresh-air kits'. These may be one deliverable named twice or two separate G.E. accessories - the possible double-count with the filter line above is stated here, not resolved. SETTLES IT: the approved G.E. accessory submittal - is there a separate fresh-air-kit part number?
lines.src: M201 PTAC notes ('low-ambient + fresh-air kits') - M201 PTAC schedule OSA column, 45.0 CFM on both PTAC-1 and PTAC-2
lines.verifyAtPunch: Open the PTAC front: outside-air damper present, moves freely, and set OPEN not shut; have T&B read outside air at the unit and record it against the scheduled 45.0 CFM.

lines.label: PTAC low-ambient kit
lines.where: Internal to the PTAC - no sheet locates it. The only place it can be confirmed in a finished room is the accessory/model label inside the front panel.
lines.instanceNote: The ITEM is well established (M201 names it plainly, and M201 gives the PTAC an operating range of 55-115 F) but no sheet says which component it is or where it can be seen. Carried IN because it is verifiable at a visible point - the label. The DB grades it HIGH, which the sheets do not support. SETTLES IT: the approved G.E. PTAC submittal accessory list matched to the installed unit's label.
lines.src: M201 PTAC notes ('low-ambient + fresh-air kits') - M201 PTAC operating range 55-115 F
lines.verifyAtPunch: Read the accessory/model label inside the PTAC front panel and WRITE THE TEXT DOWN - this is a documentation check, not a sight check; do not write it up as missing off a visual pass.

lines.label: PTAC louvered access panel
lines.where: NOT STATED BY ANY SHEET - M201 names the accessory but does not say whether it is on the unit cabinet or in the wall/enclosure.
lines.instanceNote: M201 names it in the PTAC accessory sentence and NOTHING else in the mechanical set locates or details it - M401 detail 02 and M501 detail 9 do not show it. Whether it is a G.E. accessory on the unit or an architectural wall panel is NOT STATED. The DB carries it at HIGH, which the sheets do not support. Flagged rather than dropped because if it is a wall panel it is a visible, operable item in the finished room. SETTLES IT: the approved G.E. PTAC accessory submittal - if it is a G.E. part number it is a unit accessory; if not, it is an architectural panel nobody has drawn. If absent, RECORD it against the submittal before writing it up.
lines.src: M201 PTAC notes ('louvered access panel') - against M401 detail 02 and M501 detail 9, which do not show one
lines.verifyAtPunch: Look for a louvered panel at or around the PTAC and RECORD present or absent with a photo; if present, confirm it is fastened, operable and finished.

lines.label: The two visible parts of the PTAC base condition - the PTAC edge over the carpet tile, and the ST-02 stone stool set over the unit
lines.where: At the PTAC, window wall: the carpet edge under the unit and the stone stool above it (A556 view 07 tags ST-02 at the window stool over the PTAC).
lines.instanceNote: SPLIT ROW, AND TWO SEPARATE PROBLEMS ON 238. (1) The DB row bundles the PTAC field-built sub-base - concealed under the unit and behind the drywall closure by the time the room is finished, and on the OUT list - with the two things a walker CAN see. Only the visible part is emitted. (2) NEITHER visible part is clean on A556: keynote 30 'EDGE OF PTAC ABOVE CARPET TILES' is NOT in A556's placed keynote lists (view 03 finish plan carries 22, 7 and 4 only), although A550 and A555 both place it - so the carpet-edge rule is not established for 238 by its own sheet; and A556 flag 2 records that the stool is tagged ST-02, which is NOT IN reference/finish_schedule.md at all (the schedule carries ST-01 quartz and SS-01), while A550, A551, A552, A553.2 and A555 all tag ST-01 at the identical window-stool condition. SETTLES IT: read A556 view 03 on the source PDF for keynote 30, and an RFI to MWT on ST-02 vs ST-01 before the stone is ordered. Sequence note: the stone is set AFTER the PTAC.
lines.src: M501 detail 9 (field-built sub-base, see arch) - A556 view 07 (ST-02 window stool over the PTAC) and A556 flag 2 - A550 keynote legend 30 'EDGE OF PTAC ABOVE CARPET TILES', NOT placed on A556 - AS103 drywall closure - reference/finish_schedule.md (no ST-02 card)
lines.verifyAtPunch: Confirm the PTAC edge sits ABOVE the carpet tile and not on it, that the stool is level and not bearing on the cabinet, and that the drywall closure at the sleeve gap is finished and painted - then READ THE STONE and record whether ST-02 or ST-01 was installed.

lines.label: PTAC thermostat — 7-day programmable, HARDWIRED (keynote 24 adds that thermostat-to-PTAC communication may be wireless). ONE PER PTAC, AND THIS ROOM HAS ONE PTAC — M401 states verbatim 'Each guestroom is served by a single PTAC', and A555 places keynote 1 only at the window wall, so expect ONE thermostat here
lines.where: Room wall at the PTAC / window wall. A556 places keynote 24 TWICE - on view 03 (the ELECTRICAL PLAN) and on elevation 06 (the bed wall + sofa wall). M401 KN7 and M301 GN5 defer the exact location to the architectural set.
lines.instanceNote: HEIGHT IS OPEN - coordination_issues.md C-03, and the set carries five numbers: A550/A556 keynote 24 '48" MAX TO TOP OF DEVICE'; M401 KN4 48" AFF accessible / 54" non-accessible; G402 note 11 band 15"-48"; G400 detail 02 THERMOSTAT 4'-0"; M101 N29 4'-0" AFF unless noted; and E101's symbol legend 60" (the outlier). For an accessible key the accessible sources converge at 48" MAX. DO NOT write up a height deficiency - MEASURE AND RECORD to the top of the device. M101 N29 also carries two punch-visible requirements that are easy to throw away: thermostats are NOT to go on an exterior wall if an interior wall is available, and if one IS on an exterior wall it needs an insulated backing plate behind it. On 238 keynote 24 lands on the bed/sofa wall elevation, which is an interior wall - so a stat found on the window wall is a finding, not a preference. TRADE SEAM: M101 N28 - the electrical contractor pulls the control wiring, the mechanical contractor furnishes the thermostat and terminates it.
lines.src: A556 view 03 (electrical plan) keynote 24 and A556 elevation 06 keynote 24 - A550 keynote legend 24 (verbatim) - M401 KN4 - M301 GN5 - M101 N28 / N29 - M201 PTAC notes (7-day programmable) - G402 note 11 - G400 detail 02 - E101 symbol legend - coordination_issues.md C-03
lines.verifyAtPunch: Measure to the TOP of the device and WRITE THE NUMBER DOWN against 48" MAX (keynote 24) - record, do not adjudicate, because five printed values are live. Confirm the stat is not on an exterior wall when an interior wall was available (M101 N29), and if it is on the exterior wall confirm the insulated backing plate. Call heat, then call cool, and confirm the PTAC responds each time; if the thermostat-to-PTAC link is wireless (permitted by keynote 24), cycle it twice to prove the pairing holds.

lines.label: Energy-management wall controller with occupancy sensor
lines.where: Wall-mounted at the PTAC / window wall. No mechanical sheet gives it a location of its own; A556 places only ONE control-device keynote in the room (keynote 24, on view 03 and elevation 06).
lines.instanceNote: M201's PTAC sentence names BOTH an 'energy-management wall controller w/ occupancy sensor' AND a '7-day programmable thermostat' as two phrases in one list. Whether that is ONE wall device (an EMS stat with a built-in sensor) or TWO separate wall devices is NOT STATED anywhere in the mechanical set. The architectural set places only one control device in 238, which leans to one, but that is the architect's sheet and is not conclusive. Do NOT write up a missing second wall device. SETTLES IT: the approved PTAC controls submittal - one part number or two.
lines.src: M201 PTAC notes - M301 GN5 - M401 KN4 - A556 view 03 and elevation 06 keynote 24 - M602 Final Inspection (setback controls)
lines.verifyAtPunch: COUNT the wall control devices at the PTAC - one or two - and write the number down; then leave the room with the door shut, confirm the unit goes to setback, re-enter and confirm it recovers.

lines.label: Toilet / bath exhaust air grille, 50 CFM — off-white aluminium grille per the M201 EF-1 remark codes (remark 6)
lines.where: Bathroom ceiling, in the 7'-3" AFF PT-07 painted-gypsum hard lid. A556 view 02 (RCP) places keynote 19 'TOILET EXHAUST GRILLE'.
lines.instanceNote: 'EAG-50' is a CALLOUT in M101's designation/CFM format (exhaust air grille at 50 CFM), NOT a schedule mark - M201's Titus grille schedule has NO EAG-50 row; its exhaust-air-grille entry is mark E (Titus PSS-DF, 24x24 face, 6" round neck, no damper). The crosswalk is deliberately left un-made (coordination_issues.md S-02), so do NOT check the installed grille against the 24x24 / 6" dimensions as if that were the spec. Tag recorded exactly as printed on M401.
lines.src: M401 detail 02 'QQ Acc.' (EAG-50 with VD and FD) - M201 exhaust fan schedule EF-1 remark 6 (off-white aluminium grille) - M305 exhaust riser diagrams - A556 view 02 keynote 19 - coordination_issues.md S-02
lines.verifyAtPunch: Hold a tissue to the face - it must hold against the grille unaided. Have T&B read the airflow at the face and record it against 50 CFM. Confirm the grille is square to the lid, seated tight with no gap, screws set, and the face NOT paint-blinded or fouled with joint compound.

lines.label: Aldes constant-airflow regulator at the 50 CFM ceiling exhaust inlet
lines.where: Immediately behind / above the EAG-50 grille in the bath ceiling.
lines.instanceNote: The item is real and named verbatim at every inlet M305 draws - 'CEILING GRILLE EXHAUST 50 CFM c/w ALDES CONSTANT AIRFLOW REGULATOR' - but the COUNT is not supported by its only source: M305's seven riser totals sum to 2,450 CFM = exactly 49 inlets at 50 CFM, against roughly 119 needed (115 keys + 4 ice-machine alcoves). Separately, three of the four roof fans are scheduled BELOW the riser CFM assigned to them (EF-8 200 vs 350, EF-9 300-350 vs 650, EF-11 400-450 vs 850; only EF-10/EV-6 balances). Which EV riser serves 238 is not determinable from M305 or M302 - the riser diagrams carry no room numbers. qty 1 is the per-inlet reading, not a verified count. SETTLES IT: the M-EOR's riser-vs-room-count reconciliation, plus the riser assignment for the floor-2 south-west stack.
lines.src: M305 exhaust-riser diagrams EV-1 to EV-7 (the only source) - M302 (EF-1 guest toilet exhaust, Aldes regulator at the inlet per M305) - M201 flexible duct size schedule (0-50 CFM = 4" round)
lines.verifyAtPunch: Drop the EAG-50 grille and look up the neck: RECORD whether a constant-airflow regulator is fitted, yes or no, with a photo. Do NOT call an absence a deficiency yet - the count is what the M-EOR's reconciliation is waiting on.

lines.label: Toilet exhaust fan - M201 schedules Panasonic FV-0511VK2, ceiling type, 50 CFM at 0.10 in. s.p., 115/1/60, backdraft damper, off-white aluminium grille
lines.where: Bathroom ceiling at the toilet exhaust inlet - IF it is a physical in-room fan at all.
lines.instanceNote: TWO LIVE CONFLICTS ON ONE DEVICE, BOTH RECORDED. (1) DOES A FAN EXIST AT ALL - coordination_issues.md C-06? M201 schedules EF-1 as a real Panasonic ceiling fan and M202 / M301-M304 repeat it as guest-toilet exhaust; M305's riser diagrams show each guestroom inlet as a PLAIN CEILING GRILLE + Aldes regulator on a central riser driven by roof fans EF-8 to EF-11, with no in-room fan anywhere. E400's Panel A and Panel B guestroom schedules carry NO exhaust-fan circuit, which leans grille-only but is not conclusive - M201 remark 3 would put a fan on the Lighting circuit and need no breaker. (2) IF a fan exists, WHAT SWITCHES IT? M201 EF-1 remark 3 = 'switch w/ room lights'; G402 guestroom-bath general note 3 = 'CEILING MOUNTED LIGHT FIXTURE AND FAN TO BE SWITCHED SEPARATELY FROM LIGHT'. Those two sheets disagree. Do NOT order 115 units on this. SETTLES IT: the M-EOR's answer to C-06 - and your field reading of what is behind the grille at 238.
lines.src: M201 exhaust fan schedule EF-1 (Panasonic FV-0511VK2, 50 CFM, 115/1/60, remarks 1,2,3,5,6,9) - M202 - M302 - against M305 riser diagrams (plain ceiling grille + Aldes regulator, no in-room fan) - E400 Panel A/B schedules (no exhaust-fan circuit) - G402 guestroom-bath general note 3 - coordination_issues.md C-06
lines.verifyAtPunch: Drop the bath ceiling grille and RECORD what is behind it - a fan housing, or bare duct running to a riser. If it is a fan: run it, identify WHICH switch runs it, and write down whether it is on the light switch (M201 remark 3) or on its own separate switch (G402 bath GN3); confirm the backdraft damper flaps open under flow and falls shut when the fan stops; read airflow against 50 CFM.

lines.label: Volume damper at the toilet exhaust, with a locking quadrant
lines.where: At the toilet exhaust branch above the bath ceiling. M401 detail 02 shows it with the EAG-50 and the FD but does not dimension its position; M301 N11 requires a balancing damper at each branch/runout.
lines.instanceNote: ARGUABLE SCOPE, STATED OPENLY. If the VD sits at the grille neck it is reachable by dropping the EAG-50 and is plainly IN; if it sits further up the branch it is above the 7'-3" hard PT-07 bath lid with NO access panel drawn on A556 view 02, and it becomes unreachable rough-in. No sheet says which. Carried IN because its EFFECT is tested at a visible point - the airflow reading at the grille - and because M101 N7 requires min 12"x12" access to dampers either way.
lines.src: M401 detail 02 (EAG-50 with VD and FD) - M101 legend (Manual Volume Damper VD) - M101 N25-N26 (own balancing device per outlet; manual balancing dampers have locking quadrant) - M301 N11 (balancing damper each branch/runout) - M101 N7 (min 12"x12" access to dampers)
lines.verifyAtPunch: Drop the EAG-50 and look up the neck: damper present WITH A LOCKING QUADRANT, set at a balanced position and the quadrant locked - not wired shut, taped, screwed hard open or fully closed. If no damper is visible at the neck, record that it is further up the branch and that there is no access panel to reach it.

lines.label: Wall air grille / make-up air diffuser, 30 CFM — the transfer/make-up air path to the bathroom (keynote 20, 'MAKE-UP AIR DIFFUSER')
lines.where: A556 ELEVATION 05 - the entry door / mirror wall - places keynote 20. Note that on the standard QQ sheet A555 the same keynote lands on elevation 07 (bed wall + sofa wall), so do NOT look for it where the standard rooms carry it.
lines.instanceNote: 238 IS BETTER SOURCED THAN ROOM 118 ON THIS ITEM AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS: M401 detail 02 (QQ Acc.) carries WAG-30 as make-up air to the bath, AND A556 elevation 05 places keynote 20 on 238's own sheet - two independent sources, where A552 (room 118) placed neither. What keeps this MEDIUM is the tag, not the existence: 'WAG-30' is a designation/CFM callout, not a schedule mark - M201's Titus schedule has no WAG-30 row and the crosswalk is un-made (coordination_issues.md S-02), so there is no scheduled size or model to punch the installed grille against. M301 N13 also permits a lined transfer duct OR a door undercut under 50 CFM as the alternative path.
lines.src: M401 detail 02 'QQ Acc.' (WAG-30, 30 CFM, make-up to the bath) - A556 elevation 05 keynote 20 - A550 keynote legend 20 'MAKE-UP AIR DIFFUSER' - M301 N13 - M101 legend - coordination_issues.md S-02
lines.verifyAtPunch: Find the make-up air diffuser on the entry-door / mirror wall and have T&B read it against 30 CFM, recording the number. If there is no diffuser, also measure the bath door undercut and record it against the 1/2" undercut M301 N13 allows under 50 CFM - 'no diffuser AND no undercut' is a different finding from 'no diffuser'.

lines.label: Ceiling fire / radiation damper at the rated floor-ceiling penetration — Ruskin CFD4, UL 555C, fusible link, ceramic-fibre thermal shroud, 3"x3" galvanised continuous angle to the sleeve on all four sides, sheet-metal duct throughout (flex NOT allowed)
lines.where: In the bath ceiling directly above the EAG-50 grille, on the 4" round toilet exhaust to the EV riser.
lines.instanceNote: ARGUABLE, AND EMITTED RATHER THAN DROPPED. AGAINST (out of scope): the damper body sits above the bath's 7'-3" hard PT-07 gyp lid with NO access panel drawn on A556 view 02, which matches the 'concealed rough-in' rule. FOR (in scope): M101 N7 requires min 12"x12" access to dampers, M301 Key Note 4 requires an access panel above the ceiling for HVAC maintenance, and M101 N31-N32 require approved access plus a permanent exterior label in letters at least 1/2" high reading FIRE DAMPER - the drawings themselves require it to be reachable. If there is no access, the ABSENCE is the finding and it belongs on the access-panel line below.
lines.src: M401 detail 02 (EAG-50 with VD and FD) - M301 GN3 (all HVAC penetrations of a fire-rated ceiling protected by ceiling fire dampers, UL 555) - M501 detail 2 (Ruskin CFD4, UL 555C, ceramic-fibre shroud, 3"x3" angle four sides, sheet metal not flex) - M101 N7, N31, N32 - M305 (FD at each floor penetration)
lines.verifyAtPunch: If access exists: read the label and confirm a Ruskin CFD4; fusible link intact and NOT painted, taped, wired or screwed open; ceramic-fibre shroud in place; 3"x3" angle continuous on all four sides of the sleeve; and HARD sheet metal at the damper, not flex (M501 det 2 forbids flex here). If there is NO access, stop, record that on the access-panel line and cut nothing.

lines.label: Access panel in the bath ceiling to the fire damper and the volume damper - min 12"x12", with the permanent damper label. REQUIRED BY NOTE, DRAWN ON NO GUESTROOM RCP IN THE SET
lines.where: Would be in the 7'-3" PT-07 painted-gypsum bath lid at the FD/VD above it.
lines.instanceNote: DB GAP - no access-panel row exists on 238 or on any room. The REQUIREMENT is printed; only the PLACEMENT is missing. None of the ten A550-A556 guestroom RCPs draws an access panel, A556 view 02 included (its keynotes are 18, 19, 7, 4 and the ceiling-divider note 8). The only flush-access-panel keynote anywhere in the A12x/A55x set is at the ICE-MACHINE alcove. This is a real, repeating, 115-room omission, an RFI candidate, and a CO-inspection exposure - an inspector cannot verify a damper he cannot reach. qty 1 is the requirement, not a drawn count. SETTLES IT: RFI to the M-EOR / MWT asking where the guestroom bath damper access panel goes and who cuts it.
lines.src: M101 N7 (min 12"x12" access panels to valves, traps, dampers, cleanouts, controls) - M301 Key Note 4 (access panel above ceiling for HVAC maintenance) - M101 N31-N32 (approved access + permanent exterior label, letters at least 1/2", reading FIRE DAMPER) - M501 detail 2 - against A556 view 02 (RCP - no access panel drawn or keynoted)
lines.verifyAtPunch: Look at the bath ceiling and RECORD access panel yes or no; if no, photograph the intact lid and write it up as the finding. Cut nothing.

lines.label: CONFIRM ABSENT - ceiling supply air diffuser. None is drawn in any guestroom on any mechanical sheet; the PTAC is the room's only supply
lines.where: Main room and entry-leg ceilings (A556 view 02: 8'-3 3/8" main room, 7'-3" bath and entry, all PT-07).
lines.instanceNote: ZERO-QUANTITY CONFIRM ROW. M401 detail 02 gives 238 a PTAC, a 4" fresh-air duct above the ceiling, the EAG-50 exhaust and the WAG-30 transfer - and no supply diffuser. M201's Titus schedule carries supply diffusers A/B/C/D, but M302 assigns them to the corridor off MAU-1, not to the guestrooms. So a ceiling supply diffuser in 238 would be either an unrecorded change or the corridor's air landing in the wrong place. It is graded MEDIUM rather than HIGH because the absence is read from what the sheets DO show, not from a printed statement that guestrooms have none.
lines.src: M401 detail 02 'QQ Acc.' - M302 (corridor supply from MAU-1, 'typical 2x B/90') - M201 grille & diffuser schedule - A556 view 02 (RCP)
lines.verifyAtPunch: Look up in the main room and the entry leg and confirm there is NO ceiling supply diffuser; if one IS installed, photograph it, record its size and neck, and raise it - no mechanical sheet puts supply air in a guestroom ceiling.

lines.label: Guestroom panelboard PANEL "B" - 100 A MCB, 120/208 V 1-phase 3-wire, NEMA 1, COPPER bus, Square D / GE / Cutler-Hammer
lines.where: BED WALL / SOFA WALL - A556 elevation 06 places keynote 51 and labels 'ELEC. PANEL'. Measure the control height and record it against the printed band for the configuration built (MAX 6" per A532.1 view 02, or MIN 8" / MAX 10" above the rim per A532 elevation 05). lines.label: CONFIRM ABSENT - visual notification strobes (VISUAL NOTIFICATION APPLIANCE), System Sensor SCWLED. The hearing-accessible package is 2 at 177 cd in the room plus 1 at 15 cd in the bath. EXPECT ZERO IN 238
lines.where: n/a if the expectation holds. In a hearing-accessible key they land on the room ceiling(s) and the bath ceiling.
lines.instanceNote: MOBILITY-ACCESSIBLE IS NOT HEARING-ACCESSIBLE - this is the single easiest mistake to make on an ADA room and on this key it is worth three strobes. A100's Guestroom Matrix row for 238 is 'Queen Queen ACC, CD' - the printed legend reads HA = Handicapped Accessible, HI = Hearing Impaired, CD = Connecting Door, and every HI key sits on a SEPARATE matrix row ('Queen Queen, HI'). 238's row carries no HI. INDEPENDENT SUPPORT: room 317, a mobility-accessible key with the wheelchair symbol drawn, was read off FA-3 and has NO strobes at all, while 309 - a plain Queen-Queen - carries three; the two attributes are independent. The four LOCATED hearing keys on floor 2 are 209, 213, 216 and 218, and 238 is not among them. STILL OPEN BUILDING-WIDE (coordination_issues.md C-04): 12 hearing keys required and provided per G100.2 and both matrices, only 8 located, and conflicts.md A11 point 3 records that G001's HI rows sum to 10 against a printed 12 - 'Do not order 12 hearing/visual-alarm kits off G001's room-type rows.' SETTLES IT: the FA-2 room region for 238 read at 450-500 dpi.
lines.src: FA-1 schedule row SCWLED, STROBE ONLY, CEILING, qty 80 (packages/fire-appliance.md section 2.1) - FA-3 rooms 309 and 313 (2 x 177 cd + 1 x 15 cd bath) and room 317 (mobility accessible, zero strobes) per section 2.2 - A100 GUESTROOM MATRIX row 'Queen Queen ACC, CD' and the printed HA / HI / CD legend - room_map.md (hearing-impaired symbol drawn in 213, 216, 218; 238 carries the accessible symbol only) - A550 keynote legend 43 (NOT placed on A556) - coordination_issues.md C-04 - conflicts.md A11 point 3
lines.verifyAtPunch: Confirm there are NO strobes on the room ceiling and NO strobe in the bath, and that no orphan blank plate, capped box or mounting ring is left behind in either ceiling. If strobes ARE installed, that is the finding - photograph each, read the model off the plate, RECORD THE CANDELA MARKING, and log it, because it contradicts both unit matrices and the FA-3 read of the same attribute at 317.

lines.label: CONFIRM ABSENT - carbon monoxide detector. Silent Knight SKFIRECOW is scheduled qty 3 for the whole building and none is placed in a guest room
lines.where: n/a in the guest room. FA-1's 3 units are 'LOCATE AS SHOWN ON CEILING' and their locations are not extracted.
lines.instanceNote: NOTHING IN THE SET PUTS A CO DETECTOR IN A GUEST ROOM, and guest rooms carry no fuel-fired appliance - the PTAC is electric at 208 V. FLAGGED because this is an ABSENCE, not a verified exclusion: no sheet states that guest rooms are exempt, it simply never places one. Three CO detectors on a gas-fired hotel (M301: laundry with 4 dryers at 190 MBH, water-heater room with 2 WH at 1,500 MBH) is a coverage question for the Eagle Pass AHJ under the submittal's 2018 IBC/IFC + 2019 NFPA 72 basis - that is a TCO conversation, not a room-walk one.

lines.label: Data outlet - CAT6 RJ-45, PANDUIT cable and patch cord with PANDUIT LOCKS on exposed connections, LABELLED, homerun to the floor IDF
lines.where: Per A556 view 03's device-spacing string (7'-6", 7'-4", 7'-2", 2'-2", 1'-10", 1'-2", 10"/10", 6", 3") and elevation 04. Height contested - record it.
lines.instanceNote: Keyed note 45 IS placed on A556 view 03 AND on elevation 04, so the item is sourced for 238. COUNT IS NOT STATED ANYWHERE - the DATA symbol is a graphic on A556 view 03 and E400 detail 06, and no sheet, schedule or note gives a per-room drop count; qty 1 is the placeholder. Compounding: there is NO telecom riser diagram, rack elevation, port count or patch-panel schedule anywhere in this set, so 'correctly terminated' cannot be checked against a design document - the punch reference is the low-voltage integrator's as-built, not the E-series. HEIGHT OPEN - 12" (A530-A533 GENERAL NOTES D) vs 18" (E101 symbol legend, G400 detail 02); record it, do not judge it. ON THIS KEY ONE JACK IS AN ACCESSIBILITY REQUIREMENT: A530 GENERAL NOTE G requires at least one data connection between 15" and 48" AFF with compliant clear floor area.
lines.src: A556 view 03 keyed note 45 and elevation 04 keyed note 45 - A550 keynote legend 45 (verbatim) and POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND 'DATA' - E101 GN #8 (CAT6, Panduit cable and patch cord with Panduit locks, labelled) - E101 symbol legend (data outlet 18" AFF) - G400 detail 02 (1'-6") - A530 GENERAL NOTES D (12") and G

On each: read the label and confirm it is labelled at all, confirm the cable and patch cord are PANDUIT with PANDUIT LOCKS on the exposed connections, and plug a laptop in to prove link and get an address. Measure and record each jack's centreline against the open 12"/18" split, and confirm at least ONE data connection falls inside 15"-48" AFF with clear floor area.

lines.label: TV outlet behind the television (tag 903) - CAT6 RJ-45 jack ALWAYS; coax F-connector ONLY if keyed note 47 option A governs
lines.where: Behind the TV on the working wall; keyed note 47 requires MIN 6" CLEARANCE FROM WALL BOXES. A556 view 01 tags 903 TELEVISION once.
lines.instanceNote: Keyed note 47 IS placed on A556 view 03 AND elevation 04, and tag 903 is placed once, so there is one TV location. But keyed note 47 prints an A/B OPTION and NO SHEET SELECTS ONE: A) no smart TV - COAX behind the TV plus a CAT6 RJ-45 jack in smurf tube to the WAP under the desk; B) smart/IPTV - 'COAX NOT REQ'D', CAT6 only. THE DB ROW PRESUMES OPTION A (it lists coax). The CAT6 jack is required under BOTH - punch that unconditionally, and do NOT write up a missing coax until the smart-TV question is answered, which is an owner/FF&E decision, not a drawing one. Keyed note 47's second jack is 'IN ONE-BEDROOM TV' and 238 is not a one-bedroom.
lines.src: A556 view 03 keyed note 47 and elevation 04 keyed note 47 - A550 keynote legend 47 (verbatim, both options) - A556 view 01 FF&E tag 903 TELEVISION - A550 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND 'OUTLET - TV' - E101 symbol legend (TV outlet w/ F, 18" AFF)
lines.verifyAtPunch: Pull the TV off its mount: confirm a CAT6 RJ-45 jack is present behind it - required under BOTH options and punchable unconditionally - and plug a laptop in to prove link. RECORD whether a COAX F-connector is also present and establish which option was bought BEFORE writing anything up. Confirm the smurf tube runs from behind the TV to the WAP position under the desk, that the patch cord lands on the edge controller, and that the box keeps MIN 6" clearance from adjacent wall boxes.

lines.label: Telephone outlet (tag 905) with 3/4" conduit and pull string
lines.where: Nightstand / bed area at the 905 telephone position. Height contested - record it.

The COUNT of 1 is DERIVED from the FF&E tag, not from a printed drop schedule - no sheet states per-room telephone drop counts, and 238 has TWO beds and three nightstand positions, so confirm whether one phone serves both beds. HEIGHT OPEN, 12" vs 18". THE NOTE THAT BITES ON AN ACCESSIBLE KEY: G402 general note 9 verbatim - 'PROVIDE AN ELECTRICAL OUTLET WITHIN 48" OF THE TELEPHONE CONNECTION. THE OUTLET MUST HAVE A CLEAR FLOOR SPACE AND MEET ACCESSIBILITY STANDARDS FOR REACH RANGE.'

lines.label: Wireless access point in a 3-GANG BOX MOUNTED VERTICALLY under the desk - keyed note 44 verbatim: 'WAP IN 3-GANG BOX MOUNTED VERTICALLY UNDER DESK. MAINTAIN 6" BETWEEN ALL BOXES, TYP ALL GUESTROOMS. COORDINATE WAP LOCATION WITH CASEGOODS TO AVOID CONFLICTS'

If present: box mounted VERTICALLY, at least 6" clear of every adjacent box, not buried or heat-trapped behind the casegoods, powered, status LED normal - then shut the guestroom door and confirm a phone gets internet at both beds and in the bath.

lines.label: Optional wired data connection at the desktop grommet - keyed note 46: either a CAT6 RJ-45 jack and patch cord, or a patch cord from a WAP port
lines.where: At the desktop grommet on the working-wall desk, directly above the WAP position. A556 places keyed note 46 on view 03 AND on elevation 04.

WHICH ONE WAS BOUGHT IS NOT STATED ANYWHERE (packages/electrical.md open item 6 - a x115 cost item: option A is a real jack, option B is near-zero cost). Under either option a guest must get a working wired connection at the desk, so the walker cannot mis-punch it. Do NOT call 'nothing there' a defect until the scope question is answered.

lines.label: Connected Room edge controller - the in-room head-end the TV data jack patches into. NO mark, NO symbol and NO schedule entry exists anywhere in the set
lines.where: NOT LOCATED ON ANY SHEET. The only clue is keyed note 47's own cable topology - TV CAT6 in smurf tube to the WAP under the desk, then a patch cord to the edge controller - which puts it at or near the WAP. That is inference from the cable path, not a printed location.
lines.instanceNote: The device is named twice on the drawings and drawn nowhere: keyed note 47 ends both of its options with 'PATCH CORD TO EDGE CONTROLLER FOR CONNECTED ROOM', and E101 GN #8 names 'connected room' among the exposed connections requiring Panduit locks. There is no symbol, no schedule row, no circuit and no mounting location anywhere in the E-series, so its power source and location are unstated. The punch reference is the Hilton-approved integrator's as-built. SETTLES IT: the low-voltage integrator's submittal naming the edge-controller product and its in-room location.

If nothing is there, record that too; do not write up the electrician, because no sheet places one.

lines.label: CONFIRM ABSENT - doorbell on/off switch, keyed note 28: 'DOORBELL ON/OFF SWITCH (COMMUNICATION FEATURES ROOMS ONLY) SIGNAGE AS REQ'D.' EXPECT ZERO IN 238
lines.where: Guest-room entry door GR-1 in a communication-features key; the on/off switch is an in-room device. A556 PLACES keyed note 28 TWICE - on view 03 (electrical plan) and on elevation 06 (bed wall + sofa wall).
lines.instanceNote: EXPECT ZERO - AND THIS IS A TRAP ON 238, because the DB carries a row for it AND keyed note 28 is placed twice on 238's own sheet, so a field electrician reading A556 sees a doorbell keynote on the plan and on an elevation. The keynote TEXT restricts it: 'COMMUNICATION FEATURES ROOMS ONLY'. 238 is MOBILITY-accessible with a connecting door, not hearing-accessible - A100's matrix row is 'Queen Queen ACC, CD' and the printed legend reads HA = Handicapped Accessible, HI = Hearing Impaired, CD = Connecting Door; there is no HI on that row, and every HI key sits on a separate row. The same reasoning that gives this room zero strobes gives it zero doorbell. Building-wide the communication-features register is still incomplete - 12 required, 8 located (209/213/216/218 on floor 2, 309/313/316/318 on floor 3) - and 238 is not among the located four on its own floor (coordination_issues.md C-04). qty 0 = confirm absent, and check specifically for a doorbell that should not be there.

lines.verifyAtPunch: Check the corridor face of the entry door GR-1 for a doorbell push and the inside of the room for an on/off switch and confirm NEITHER is present, with no orphan blank plate, capped box or filled hole at either location. If one IS installed, photograph it and log it - keyed note 28 restricts the doorbell to communication-features rooms and 238 is not one.
